questions.question: Viceroy Curzon partitioned Bengal in ___________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1905**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

Partition of Bengal:

__
 
• In 1905 Viceroy Curzon partitioned Bengal.
 
• At that time Bengal was the biggest province of British India and included Bihar and parts of Orissa.
 
• The Partition of Bengal was carried out on 16 October 1905 which resulted in the division of Bengal into Eastern Bengal and Western Bengal.
 
• The British argued for dividing Bengal for reasons of administrative convenience.
 
 
• But what did “administrative convenience” mean? Whose “convenience” did it represent? Clearly, it was closely tied to the interests of British officials and businessmen.
 
• Even so, instead of removing the non-Bengali areas from the province, the government separated East Bengal and merged it with Assam.
 
 
 
• Perhaps the main British motives were to curtail the influence of Bengali politicians and to split the Bengali people.
 
• The partition of Bengal infuriated people all over India.
 
• All sections of the Congress – the Moderates and the Extremist, as they may be called – opposed it. 
 
• Moderates such as Surendranath Banerjee, K.K.Mitra led an anti-partition campaign.
 
• They followed petition, prayer, and protest methods.
 
• Meetings were held all over Bengal and a decision was taken to boycott the foreign goods.
 
• The message to Boycott the Manchester cloth and Liverpool salt was spread throughout Bengal by the leaders.
 
• The Indian National Congress under the leadership of Gopal Krishna Gokhale rejected the Partition of Bengal and resolved to support the Swadeshi movement

 and boycott.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

The Administration division:

__
 
• On the linguistic basis: Reducing the Bengalis to a minority in Bengal itself. The new proposal of Bengal was provisioned to have 17 million Bengalis and 37 million Hindi and Oriya speakers.
 
• Based on religion: The Western Bengal was to be a Hindu majority area (It was almost 42 million out of a total 54 million) and the Eastern Bengal was to be a Muslim majority area (It was almost 18 million out of a total of 31 million).

Thus, in 1905 Viceroy Curzon partitioned Bengal.__

​ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f4bcdf5abc29b16ec94bdc28a4b074a49eecc2b05dbafce3079de096190472ec.png]

questions.question: The process of depositing a layer of zinc on iron is called __________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is galvanization.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Galvanization is the process of depositing a layer of zinc on iron.
 
• During Galvanization, zinc is used for coating iron and steel objects, preventing them from rusting.​

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
 

 Process
 Description
 
 
 
 

 Filtration
 Filtration is a separation process in which a filter is used to remove solid particles from a fluid (liquid or gas) by passing the fluid through a porous medium. The filter allows the fluid to pass through while trapping the solid particles. It is commonly used in water treatment, air purification, and in the food and beverage industry.
 
 

 Sedimentation
 Sedimentation is a physical water treatment process used to settle out suspended solids in water under the influence of gravity. The solid particles (sediment) settle at the bottom of a container. In water and wastewater treatment processes, sedimentation tanks, or clarifiers, facilitate the removal of solids.
 
 

 Crystallisation
 Crystallization is a separation technique that is used to separate a solid that has dissolved in a liquid and made a solution. The solution is warmed in an open container, allowing the solvent to evaporate, leaving a saturated solution. As the solution cools, the solid begins to crystallize out, and then it can be collected and dried. Crystallisation is often used in chemistry to purify substances.

questions.question: Prithviraja III defeated Afghan ruler sultan Muhammad Ghori in ___________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1191**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The best-known Chahamana ruler was Prithviraj III (1168- 1192), who defeated an Afghan ruler named Sultan Muhammad Ghori in 1191, but lost to him the very next year, in 1192.
 
• Mohammad Ghori’s invasion (1175 AD-1206 AD):
 
 
• Mohammad Ghori invaded India and laid the foundation of Muslim domination in India.
 
• He is often considered the founder of Muslim rule in India.
 
 

 
• Battle of Tarain:

 
 
• In the first battle of Tarain was fought in 1191 the Ghori Forces were completely rooted out by Prithviraj Chauhan.
 
• The second battle of Tarain was fought in 1192 in which Prithviraj Chauhan was defeated by Ghori.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Prithviraja III

 
• Prithviraja III was the best-known Chahamana ruler.
 
• From 1177 to 1192 CE, Prithviraja III, sometimes referred to as Prithviraj Chauhan or Rai Pithora, ruled Sapadalaksha.
 
• He belonged to the Chauhan (Chahamana) dynasty, and his capital was Ajmer in modern-day Rajasthan. In 1177 CE, when Prithviraj ascended the throne as a boy, he inherited a kingdom that ran from Thanesar in the north to Jahazpur (Mewar) in the south.
 
• He sought to enlarge this realm by engaging in military operations against nearby countries, most notably by defeating the Chandelas.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT one of the three main parts of cell?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Vacuole**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The function of the vacuole in plants -
 
 
• The vacuole plays a major role in the rapid flow of water by the cell.
 
• The vacuole provides mechanical force to the colloid matrix found in the cytoplasm of the cell.
 
• The vacuole helps in osmoregulation. (Unicellular Organisms)
 
• Vacuoles participate in photosynthesis activities such as CAM (Cressulian Acidata Bolism) plant.
 
• Vacuole regulates the turgor pressor in higher grade plants and keeps the cell Turgid.
 
• The vacuole removes toxins and some secondary metabolites from metabolism.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
 

 Component
 Description
 Function
 
 
 
 

 Nucleus
 The nucleus is a highly specialized organelle that serves as the information processing and control center of the cell. It contains most of the cell's genetic material organized as DNA molecules, along with proteins, to form chromosomes.
 The nucleus controls and regulates the activities of the cell (e.g., growth, metabolism) and carries the genes, structures that carry hereditary information. It is also responsible for the synthesis of ribosomes, the protein factories of a cell.
 
 

 Cytoplasm
 The cytoplasm is the jelly-like substance within the cell, nestled between the cell membrane and the nucleus. It contains all the organelles, like mitochondria, ribosomes, endoplasmic reticulum, etc. The cytoplasm is made up of cytosol - a gel-like substance within which all the other cellular components are suspended.
 The cytoplasm is responsible for giving a cell its shape and helping the parts within it move. It also helps in the dissolution of cellular waste. Various metabolic reactions, such as protein synthesis, occur in the cytoplasm.
 
 

 Cell Membrane (Plasma Membrane)
 The cell membrane, also known as the plasma membrane, is a thin lipid bilayer (made up of two layers of fat cells) that surrounds all cells and separates the cell's interior from its outside environment. It is selectively permeable and controls the movement of substances in and out of cells.
 The main function of the cell membrane is to protect the cell from its surroundings. It provides a fixed environment inside the cell and regulates the movement of substances, allowing some substances to cross it while stopping others.

questions.question: Part IV of the Indian constitution provides for ____________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Directive Principles of State policy**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Part IV (Article 36-51) of the Indian Constitution is related to Directive Principles of our State Policy.
 
• It is not enforceable by any court but these are fundamental in the governance of the country.
 
• It is the duty of the government to apply these principles in law-making.
 
• These principles have been taken from the Constitution of Ireland.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
 

 Topic
 Description
 
 
 
 

 Fundamental Duties
 Fundamental Duties were added to the Indian Constitution by the 42nd Amendment in 1976, upon the recommendations of the Swaran Singh committee. There are 11 duties listed in Article 51A, which every citizen is morally obligated to perform. These duties include respecting the Constitution, national flag, and national anthem, protecting sovereignty and integrity of India, promoting harmony, preserving rich heritage, protecting the natural environment, developing a scientific temper, and upholding ideals of the freedom struggle.
 
 

 Fundamental Rights
 Fundamental Rights are defined as the basic human rights enshrined in the Constitution of India (Part III, Articles 12 to 35). These rights ensure equality, freedom, protection against discrimination, and right to constitutional remedies among others. They protect citizens against the arbitrary and absolute exercise of power by the State and ensure the democratic ethos of the country.
 
 

 Union Executive
 The Union Executive consists of the President, the Vice-President, the Prime Minister, the Council of Ministers, and the Attorney General of India. The Union Executive is responsible for the implementation of laws and policies adopted by the Parliament. The President of India is the head of the Union Executive, acting upon the advice of the Prime Minister and the Council of Ministers. The Attorney General is the chief legal advisor to the Government of India.

questions.question: Which of the following is not a valid stroke in a swimming competition?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Leg Stroke**__. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Leg Stroke: **
 
• This is not a recognized stroke style in competitive swimming.
 
• Though kicking is a fundamental part of most strokes, it is never performed alone in competitions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Breaststroke:**

 
 
• In this type of stroke, the swimmer swims on his chest, and the torso does not rotate.
 
• The legs kick out in a kind of "froggy" style while the hands pull through the water in a circle in front of the body.
 
• The swimmer breathes at the end of each cycle.
 
 
 
• **Front Stroke (or Freestyle/ Front Crawl):**
 
 
• This is commonly referred to as freestyle stroke, and it is the fastest swimming stroke.
 
• It's characterized by the swimmer being on his belly and alternating the arms for strokes while the legs perform a flutter kick.
 
 
 
• **Backstroke:**
 
 
• Also known as the back crawl, swimmers do this stroke on their backs.
 
• It involves flutter kicking in the water while rotating the arms in a windmill motion.
 
• It is the only regulated stroke to be swum on the back, and breathing is not restricted because the swimmer's face stays above water.

questions.question: Under 'SAMRIDDHI 2022-23 (Strengthening & Augmentation of Municipal Revenue for Infrastructure Development in Delhi)', people will be able to pay only the principal amount of the current and pending tax of past ___________ years for residential properties.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**five**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• On October 25, Delhi Lieutenant Governor Vinai Kumar Saxena launched a one-time property tax amnesty scheme "SAMRIDDHI 2022-23", saying it will provide a major relief to lakhs of residential and commercial property owners in the city.
 
• SAMRIDDHI, an acronym for Strengthening and Augmentation of Municipal Revenue for Infrastructure Development in Delhi, will start on October 26 and end on March 31, 2023, with no further extensions.
 
• Under the scheme, residential property owners can pay just the principal property tax amount of the current and of the past five years. For commercial properties, owners can pay the principal amount case of the last six years and get a waiver on past pending dues, including penalty and interest, according to an official statement.
 
• The L-G said SAMRIDDHI 2022-23 is a people-friendly initiative of the Municipal Corporation of Delhi which will provide a big relief to the residents and encourage property owners to get rid of long-pending disputes and related harassment.
 
• This new amnesty scheme will also widen the tax base and enable MCD to build a proper tax database by being more pragmatic about the enforcement of its long-pending tax dues.

questions.question: Those organisms which take food synthesized by plants are called ___________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Heterotrophs**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Those organisms which take food synthesized by plants are called Heterotrophs.
 
• The term "heterotroph" includes organisms that cannot synthesize their own food and rely on complex organic substances for nutrition.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Phototrophic:**

 
 
• These are organisms that carry out photosynthesis to acquire energy.
 
• They utilize sunlight, carbon dioxide, and water to produce glucose – their energy source.
 
• This group includes most plants and some bacteria and protists.
 
 
 
• **Autotrophs:**
 
 
• Autotrophs are organisms that can produce their own food from the substances available in their surroundings using light (photosynthesis) or chemical energy (chemosynthesis).
 
• Examples include plants, algae, and some types of bacteria.
 
 
 
• **Saprotrophs: **
 
 
• These are organisms that feed on dead and decaying organic matter by secreting enzymes into the environment and breaking down the organic matter into smaller particles which they then absorb.
 
• Fungi and bacteria are common examples of saprotrophs (also called saprophytes or decomposers).

questions.question: "Agricultural Census" is conducted in India at an interval of _________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __5 Years.__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• Agriculture Census forms part of a broader system of collection of Agricultural Statistics.
 
• It is a large-scale statistical operation for the collection and derivation of quantitative information about the structure of agriculture.
 
• Agricultural Census is the main source of information on a variety of agricultural parameters at a relatively minute level
 
• Through Agriculture Census it is endeavoured to collect basic data on important aspects of the agricultural economy for all the operational holdings in the country. 
 
• It collects data such as
 
 
• Number and area of ​​operational holdings,
 
• Farm size,
 
• Class-wise distribution,
 
• Land use,
 
• Tenancy,
 
• Cropping pattern
 
• Use of fertilizers, insecticides etc.,
 
 
 
• The Agriculture Census in India is conducted at an interval of five years following broad guidelines of the decennial World Census of Agriculture (WCA) evolved by the Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO) of the United Nations.
 
• Entire Census operation is conducted in three phases
 
• Operational holding is taken as a statistical unit at micro level for data collection.
 
• The aggregation of data is done at various levels of administrative units.
 
• India's first ever comprehensive Agricultural Census was carried out with the agricultural year 1970-71 as the reference

questions.question: The forces which work on the surface of the earth are called _____________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**exogenic forces**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

Exogenic Forces:

__
 
• Exogenic forces are those forces that derive their strength from the earth’s exterior or originated within the earth’s atmosphere.
 
• The forces that work on the surface of the earth are called Exogenic forces.
 
• Examples of forces: the wind, waves, water, etc.
 
• Examples of exogenic processes: weathering, mass movement, erosion, and deposition.
 
• Exogenic forces are mainly land-wearing forces.​

​ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/6d499940e4662a325cc8f0ea4c7c030e513a3e7ed52d95318f6a483c230421bc.png] 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Endogenic Forces:

 
• Endogenic forces are those internal forces that derive their strength from the earth’s interior.
 
• The forces which act in the interior of the earth are called Endogenic forces.
 
• They play a crucial role in shaping the earth's crust.
 
• The endogenic forces are mainly land-building forces.
 
• Examples: mountain-building forces, continent building forces, earthquakes, volcanism, etc.
 
• Endogenic forces sometimes produce sudden movements, like earthquakes and volcanoes.
 
• Sudden movements cause mass destruction over the surface of the earth.
 
• These at other times produce slow movements.

questions.question: In which of the following decades, there was a negative growth rate in Indian population?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is "__1911 - 1921__".

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• According to the most recent census, India's population has grown, yet between 1911 and 1921, it actually decreased.
 
• Before 1921, both male and female children had poor life expectancy rates at birth.
 
• Famines and epidemics were the leading causes of population reduction.
 
• Famine, pestilence, and influenza deaths slowed the country's population growth.
 
• There was an *increase in population* from 1901 to 1911.
 
• Due to the absence of famines and epidemics during this time, resulting in a significant* drop* in the country's death rate, the population expanded by roughly 158 lakh.
 
• However, between *1911 and 1921*, the nation's growth rate slowed.
 
• The 1918 influenza outbreak contributed to a rise in mortality and the death of *140 lakh people* nationwide.
 
• *Famine*, the *plague*, and *malaria* were further factors in the population reduction.
 
• The year 1951 is frequently referred to as the year of the population explosion since there was a significant* increase in population *after 1951.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Growth of Population 

​Phase I 

 
• The period from 1901-1921 is referred to as a period of the stagnant or stationary phase of growth of India’s population, since in this period growth rate was very low, even recording a negative growth rate during 1911-1921.
 
• Both the birth rate and death rate were high keeping the rate of increase low.
 
• Poor health and medical services, illiteracy of people at large, and inefficient distribution system of food and other basic necessities were largely responsible for high birth and death rates in this period.

Phase II 

 
• The decades 1921-1951 are referred to as the period of steady population growth.
 
• An overall improvement in health and sanitation throughout the country brought down the mortality rate.
 
• At the same time, better transport and communication systems improved distribution systems.
 
• The crude birth rate remained high in this period leading to a higher growth rate than the previous phase.
 
• This is impressive in the backdrop of the Great Economic Depression, the 1920s, and World War II.

Phase III 

 
• The decades 1951-1981 are referred to as the period of population explosion in India, which was caused by a rapid fall in the mortality rate but a high fertility rate of population in the country.
 
• The average annual growth rate was as high as 2.2 percent.
 
• It is in this period, after the Independence, that developmental activity was introduced through a centralized planning process and the economy started showing up ensuring the improvement of the living conditions of people at large.
 
• Consequently, there was a high natural increase and a higher growth rate.
 
• Besides, increased international migration bringing in Tibetans, Bangladeshis, Nepalese and even people from Pakistan contributed to the high growth rate.

Phase IV 

 
• In the post-1981 till present, the growth rate of country’s population though remained high, has started slowing down gradually.
 
• A downward trend of crude birth rate is held responsible for such population growth.
 
• This was, in turn, affected by an increase in the mean age at marriage, improved quality of life particularly education of females in the country.
 
• The growth rate of population is, however, still high in the country, and it has been projected by World Development Report that the population of India will touch 1,350 million by 2025.

questions.concept: India under East India Company’s Rule
questions.question: Which among the following Acts established the dual system of control by the British government and the East India Company in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Pitt's India Act, 1784**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Pitts India Act 1784:

 
 
• It is also known as the East India Company Act 1784__.
 
• Acts established the dual system of control by the British government and the East India Company in India
 
• It established an authority in England to supervise the company's affairs. This is known as the Board of Control which has 6 members.
 
• Governor-General in the council has more powers over Bombay and Madras Governors in matters related to the War, Revenue and Diplomacy.
 
• In India, the strength of the executive council was reduced from four to three.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• Government of India Act 1858:

 
 
• This act is also known as Act for the Betterment of India.
 
• Abolished Board of Directors and Council of Directors, thus ended dualism in Indian administration.
 
• It provided for the Secretary of State for India who would be a member of the British Cabinet.
 
• Governor-General of India as representing the Crown became known as the Viceroy of India.
 
• This act provided that the authority and the dignity of the rulers could be maintained and it put an end to further annexation and conquest.
 
 
 
• Charter Act of 1833:
 
 
• This act is also known as Saint Helena Act 1833.
 
• Lord William Bentick became the first governor-general of India.
 
• 4th member was added as a law member in the council of governor-general but only for the purpose of the legislation as a temporary member. (Lord Macaulay was the first law member)
 
• Bombay and Madras were deprived of their power to legislate.
 
• Act legalized the British colonization of the country.
 
• Law Commission was organized under Lord Macaulay to codify all Indian laws.
 
• Complete abolition of monopoly even in terms of tea and china trade.
 
 
 
• Charter Act of 1853:
 
 
• It laid down a provision that there could be open competition for ICS.
 
• Law member was made full-fledged members of the council.
 
• For the purpose of the legislation, the council was expanded by six additional members.
 
• The legislative and executive functions of the Governor-General’s council were separated for the first time.

questions.question: In Badminton, the length and width of the doubles court shall be of ______________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**13.40 m × 6.10 m**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• 13.40 m × 6.10m is the official dimension for badminton doubles court.
 
• The length of the court is 13.40 meters, and the width is 6.10 meters.
 
• These dimensions are set by the Badminton World Federation (BWF) and are followed in all official tournaments.
 
• The court has a center line that divides it into two equal halves, and there are service boxes marked on both sides.
 
• The net is placed in the center, and its height is 1.55 meters at the edges and 1.524 meters in the center.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

**Badminton Overview:**

 
• Sport Type: Racquet sport played using racquets to hit a shuttlecock across a net.
 
• Team Members: Can be played as singles (one player per side) or doubles (two players per side).
 
• Equipment: Shuttlecock and racquet.
 
• Playing Area: Played on a rectangular indoor court.
 
• Objective: Points are scored by hitting the shuttlecock with the racquet and making it land within the opponent's half of the court.
 
• Shuttlecock: A feathered or plastic projectile that decelerates rapidly due to its design.
 
• Origin: Developed in British India from the earlier game of battledore and shuttlecock. Became popular in Asia, especially in China.
 
• Olympic Debut: Introduced in the Summer Olympics in 1992 with events like men's singles, women's singles, men's doubles, and women's doubles. Mixed doubles was added later.
 
• Physical Demands: Requires aerobic stamina, agility, strength, speed, and precision. It's also a technical sport demanding good motor coordination.

**Court Dimensions:**

 
• Full Width: 6.1 metres (20 feet) for doubles and 5.18 metres (17.0 feet) for singles.
 
• Full Length: 13.4 metres (44 feet).
 
• Net Height: 1.55 metres (5 feet 1 inch) at the edges and 1.524 metres (5.00 feet) in the center.

• Shinzo Abe, Japan’s longest-serving prime minister, died after being shot while giving a campaign speech.
 
• Mr. Abe, who was 67 years old, was prime minister until late 2020 and was one of Japan’s best-known politicians.

• He was the de facto leader of the largest faction in the ruling Liberal Democratic Party and wielded strong influence in the government despite standing down as prime minister in September 2020.

questions.question: Which among the famous novels is written by Indian author R. K. Narayan?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**The dark room**__. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **"The Dark Room" by R.K. Narayan**:

 
 
• This is one of the celebrated works of the famous Indian English novelist, **R.K. Narayan.**
 
• Set in British India, it tells the story of a **submissive wife, Savitri, and her self-centered, oppressive husband, Ramani.**
 
• Savitri's inner turmoil and despair reflect the status of women in Indian society during that period.
 
• **Rasipuram Krishnaswami Iyer Narayanaswami (R.K. Narayan)** was a leading author of early Indian literature in English.
 
• He is known for his series of novels set in the fictional South Indian town of **Malgudi.**
 
• His other noteworthy works include **"Swami and Friends", "The Guide", and "The Man-Eater of Malgudi".**
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **"A Suitable Boy" by Vikram Seth:**

 
 
• This is one of the longest novels ever published in a single volume in the English language.
 
• Vikram Seth is an Indian novelist and poet.
 
• He has written several other novels and poetry collections, including **"An Equal Music", "Two Lives", and "The Golden Gate".**
 
 
 
• **"Unaccustomed Earth" by Jhumpa Lahiri: **
 
 
• This is a collection of short stories by Jhumpa Lahiri, which takes its name from a story in the book.
 
• The stories in the collection mostly focus on second-generation Indian American immigrants and their struggle to balance their cultural heritage with the pressures of living in America.
 
• Jhumpa Lahiri is a Pulitzer Prize-winning author known for her profound and poignant narratives of Indian American experiences.
 
• Her other works include** "Interpreter of Maladies", "The Namesake", and "The Lowland".**
 
 
 
• **"Half Girlfriend" by Chetan Bhagat: **
 
 
• This is a coming-of-age novel that tells the story of a rural Bihari boy named Madhav who falls in love with a rich Delhi girl named Riya. 
 
• Chetan Bhagat is a popular contemporary Indian author, known for his English-language novels about young, middle-class Indians.

questions.question: The festival of Navroz or nowroj is celebrated as new year of which community?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Parsi**__. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Parsi**:

 
 
• The festival of** Navroz (or Nowruz)** is celebrated as the** New Year by the Parsi community**.
 
• Parsis follow **Zoroastrianism**, which was founded in **ancient Persia (now Iran)**.
 
• **Navroz, or Nowruz,** means **"new day"** and it marks the first day of the Persian calendar.
 
• It usually falls on March 21, symbolizing the renewal of nature and life.
 
• The festival is marked by** feasting, praying, and meeting family and friends.**
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Buddhist: **

 
 
• The New Year in the Buddhist tradition varies depending on the country and tradition.
 
• For example, in Theravada countries, the New Year is celebrated for three days from the** first full moon day in April**.
 
 
 
• **Sindhi: **
 
 
• **The Sindhi New Year **is celebrated on the second day of the lunar month Cheti, which usually falls in late March or early April, and is known as Cheti Chand.
 
• It is celebrated in** honor of the birth of the Sindhi patron saint Jhulelal**. 
 
 
 
• **Jainism:**
 
 
• **The Jain New Year **starts right after Diwali, one of the most important festivals in India, and it generally falls in late October or early November.
 
• It marks the anniversary of the attainment of **moksha (liberation) by Mahavira, the last of the Jain Tirthankaras.**
 
• Jainism is an ancient Indian religion emphasizing non-violence and asceticism.

questions.question: In national income accounting, GVA stands for ___________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Gross Value added**__. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Gross Value Added (GVA) **is a measure in **economics** used to gauge the total productivity and economic output of a region, country or specific sector of the economy.
 
• It calculates **the value of goods and services** produced in an area, industry or sector of an economy.
 
• GVA is a measure of the **value of goods and services produced in an area, industry or sector of an economy.**
 
• It is used in the production approach to** calculating GDP (Gross Domestic Product), with the formula**:
 
• **GDP = GVA + (Taxes on Products - Subsidies on Products)**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• In accordance with the formula,** the GDP and GVA **are connected via the net taxes (which is taxes on products minus subsidies).
 
• Put simply, **GVA** is the total value of the **goods and services a sector**,** industry or region produces**, but it doesn't account for the costs of goods and raw materials that were consumed in production.
 
• Therefore, it can be considered a measure of the gross contribution to the economy of each individual producer, industry or sector.

questions.question: As per census 2011, what is the position of Uttar Pradesh with respect to the total population of India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**First**__. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **According to the 2011 Census of India,** **Uttar Pradesh** is the most populated state in India.
 
• With a population of approximately **199.8 million**, it constitutes more than **16% of the country's total population.**
 
• Here are some additional interesting facts from the** 2011 Indian Census:**
 
 
• **Population Growth: **India's population grew by 17.64% from the previous census in 2001, reaching 1.21 billion people in 2011.
 
• **Gender Ratio: **The census indicated an improvement in the sex ratio, which stood at 943 females per 1,000 males in 2011, an increase from 933 in 2001.
 
• **Literacy Rate:** The literacy rate increased to 74.04%, with male literacy at 82.14% and female literacy at 65.46%.
 
• **Urbanization:** The urban population increased to 31.16% from 27.81% in 2001.
 
• **Child Sex Ratio:** However, the child sex ratio (0-6 years) showed a decline from 927 girls per 1,000 boys in 2001 to 919 girls for every 1,000 boys in 2011, a matter of national concern.
 
• **State population:** After Uttar Pradesh, Maharashtra came as the second most populated state, followed by Bihar, West Bengal, and Andhra Pradesh.
 
• **Densely Populated State:** As per the census, Bihar was the most densely populated state with 1,106 people per square kilometer, higher than the national average of 382.

questions.question: The Brihadeshwara temple at Tanjore was built by _________ rulers.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Chola rulers**__. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Brihadeshwara Temple, also known as the Big Temple, is located in Thanjavur (formerly Tanjore) in the Indian state of Tamil Nadu.
 
• This temple was built by the Chola dynasty ruler, Raja Raja Chola I, and its construction was completed in 1010 AD.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **The Chola Dynasty**, one of the longest-ruling dynasties in **Southern India, **flourished from the **9th to the 13th century.**
 
• **The Chola Empire** extended throughout** Southern India** and the **eastern and western parts of the Indian Ocean,** which made it a significant naval and military power.
 
• **King Vijayalaya Chola,** who ruled in the late 9th century, is considered the** founder of the Chola Empire.**
 
• **The Golden Age of the Cholas** was under the** rule of Rajaraja Chola I and his son Rajendra Chola I.**
 
• **Rajaraja Chola I **constructed **the Brihadeshwara** Temple in Thanjavur, one of the **largest **and **tallest temples** in India.
 
• Its construction was completed in 1010 AD.
 
• They developed an efficient system of administration and established a centralized form of government.
 
• The Cholas had a well-structured and powerful navy, which they used for trade and conquests along the coasts of the Indian Ocean.
 
• Their rule marked a high point in** Dravidian architecture, education, literature, and the arts. Chola bronzes, intricate sculptures typically depicting Hindu gods and goddesses, are particularly famous.**
 
• **The Cholas **were patrons of Tamil literature, and it flourished during their reign.
 
• But they also encouraged** regional literature, particularly Sanskrit.**
 
• Their decline started in the **13th century, culminating with the invasion of the Delhi Sultanate.**
